I have been farming this land for 30 years, so I mostly do what worked last year. My 10.1 mu is split — I keep about 2 mu for chili because it brings cash, and the other 8.1 mu I run wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as my neighbors.

For wheat, I plant an improved variety like Jimai 22 that the dealer in town sells. I use about 50 jin (25 kg) of seed per mu. Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer 15-15-15, around 50 kg per mu as base fertilizer — that gives me roughly 7-8 kg N, same P and K. Then at jointing in spring I top-dress urea, about 20 kg per mu, that's another 9 kg N. Total nitrogen around 16-17 kg per mu. I irrigate at sowing, before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling — four times with the well. I spray once against aphids and powdery mildew, sometimes twice if I see it spreading. I plough before wheat because the stubble needs burying. I expect around 500 kg per mu, like last year.

For maize after wheat, no time to plough, I plant directly into the stubble — no-tillage with the seeder. Zhengdan 958 or a similar hybrid, everyone around here uses it. Base fertilizer compound 40 kg per mu at sowing, then urea 25 kg per mu at big trumpet stage. That's about 17 kg N total. Two irrigations usually enough — at sowing if dry, and at tasseling. One spray for corn borer. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For chili, this is where I spend the money because the price pays off. I buy hybrid seedlings from the nursery. I put chicken manure 1500 kg per mu before transplanting, plus compound fertilizer 50 kg. Then I top-dress urea and potassium sulfate two-three times during the season. Nitrogen close to 25 kg per mu, potassium heavy at 18 kg because chili needs it for fruit. I irrigate 8 times with the well, chili cannot go dry. Spray 6 times — aphids, thrips, anthracnose, the pests come one after another. I rotary till before planting. Dry chili 250 kg per mu is my target.

I spend more on chili because the return is better, and I keep wheat-maize costs steady — no point experimenting on the grain when prices are flat.
